name: Haeinsa Temple Janggyeong Panjeon, the Depositories for the Tripitaka Koreana Woodblocks
description: High on Mount Gaya in South Korea, the Haeinsa temple guards the Tripitaka Koreana, a complete set of Buddhist scriptures carved onto about 80,000 woodblocks in the 13th century. They are kept in long 15th-century halls, the Janggyeong Panjeon, whose clever design has protected the wood for over 600 years. The blocks are admired as art as well as text.
